ribhu:
[Ri+bhū+ḍu(thoma)]  CL=8 Deva/celestial being
Etymology: From Tikaṇḍa text: 'rikāro devamātā siyā' (ri refers to the mother of devas)
[Reference: Cintāmaṇi.Ṭī.6]
Sanskrit form: Ṛbhu
ricchā: [Rica+cha+ā] (thī) CL=7 Exemption, Out of stock, Not comparing, Perfection
ripu:
[Rapa+u]  CL=7 Enemy, adversary, foe
Etymology: From 'rapatyavaṇaṃ rajate' - that which attacks/opposes
Grammatical note: "u" is added (u ittaṃ)
[Reference: Dhāna.Ṭī.394]
Various forms:
- Sanskrit: ripu
- Prakrit: riu, ripu, rivu
rite:
[Rita+e(ke)]  CL=9 Without, excluding, apart from, except
Etymology: vinā = vajjanaṃ (meaning to exclude, to be without)
[Reference: Kappaduma 6]
Forms:
- Sanskrit: vinā
- Prakrit: khite
- Ardhamagadhi: khite
ritta:
[Rica+ta]  CL=9 1. Primary meanings:
(a) Empty, void, vacant, hollow
(b) Devoid of essence, meaningless, insubstantial
(c) Isolated, separated, apart
Sanskrit: rikta
Prakrit/Ardhamagadhi: ritta
2. Secondary meaning:
Abandoned, rejected, discarded
3. Noun form:
An oar, paddle (nautical term
rittahattha: [Ritta+hattha]  CL=8 Empty-handed, going without anything in hand
rittakumbhī:
[Ritta+kumbhī] (thī) CL=9 Ritta + Kumbha (masc)/Kumbbhī (fem)
Ritta (adj) empty, Kumbha (masc) /Kumbbhī (fem) clay pot; water jar; pitcher
Rittakumbhī (fem) emptied clay pot
rittakumbhūpama: [Rittakumbhī+upamā] (ti) CL=7 For example, just like an empty pot.
rittapatta:
[Ritta+patta]  CL=8 1. An empty alms bowl
2. One who has an empty alms bowl (when used as an adjective describing a bhikkhu)
rittapesuṇa: [Ritta+pesuṇa]  CL=9 One who has abandoned/given up slander and malicious speech; one who has renounced divisive speech.
rittapotthaka: [Ritta+potthaka] (pu,na) CL=10 (synonym) Rittakapotthaka (m, nt) empty book; blank manuscript
rittapurisa: [Ritta+purisa]  CL=8 A person who is empty/void of (completely lacking) jhāna, magga, and phala attainments.
rittassāda: [Ritta+assāda]  CL=8 lack of enjoyment, no enjoyment.
rittāsana: [Ritta+āsana] (na) CL=7 A place free from the five senses.
riñcitvā: [Rica+tvā] (kri,vi) CL=7 Riñcitvā-sakkata-piṭaka.] abandoned. Riñcati , see also
riṭṭha: [Risa+ta] (na) CL=7 Riḍa-saṃ. Riṭṭha-prā, addhamāgadhī.] (1) Evil. (2) Woe. Unsightly.
